doc_name: Fencing at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's masters foil
text: The men's masters foil was one of three fencing events at the 1896 Summer Olympics programme and was the sole event featuring professional athletes, taking place immediately after the amateur event on 7 April. It consisted of a single match between Leonidas Pyrgos of Greece and Joanni Perronet of France, which Pyrgos won 3–1, becoming the first Greek champion in the modern Olympics. This was the first time the event was held and it occurred only once more in Olympic history. Fencing masters were an exception to the early Olympics' amateurs-only policy, with the men's foil masters event held in 1896 and all three weapons for men, plus a special épée match between top professionals and amateurs, in 1900. By 1904, only amateur events were conducted. With only two fencers, the competition involved a single bout to three touches, following standard foil rules: touches had to be made with the tip of the foil, the target area was the torso, and priority determined the winner in cases of double touches. The exact start time of the master's event is unknown, but fencing began at 10 a.m. on the second day of events with the amateur men's foil and followed with the master's foil. The Official Report states that fencing ended at noon. Pyrgos won the only bout, 3–1.
